prcp-7days.png.summary: Most of central and southern Lower Michigan received less than 0.01 inch. Northern Lower Michigan generally received 0.01–0.25 inch. The Upper Peninsula was wetter toward the east, where parts received roughly 0.25–0.5 inch.
prcp-7days.png.basis: Visual description of the saved MRCC map. Regional values are approximate color-band readings, not station measurements.

prcp-30days.png.summary: The Upper Peninsula generally received 0.5–2 inches. Much of northern and central Lower Michigan received 1.5–3 inches. Southern and southwestern Lower Michigan were wetter, commonly 3–6 inches.
prcp-30days.png.basis: Visual description of the saved MRCC map. Regional values are approximate color-band readings, not station measurements.

prcp-90days.png.summary: The Upper Peninsula generally received 4–10 inches. Lower Michigan commonly received 7.5–15 inches, with wetter areas in the northeast and across parts of the south.
prcp-90days.png.basis: Visual description of the saved MRCC map. Regional values are approximate color-band readings, not station measurements.

prcpdev-7days.png.summary: Almost all of Michigan is in the white legend bands, representing precipitation departures within about one inch of the 1991–2020 normal. The map does not distinguish negative and positive values within these white bands.
prcpdev-7days.png.basis: Visual description of the saved MRCC map. Regional values are approximate color-band readings, not station measurements.

prcpdev-30days.png.summary: The Upper Peninsula was generally 2–4 inches below normal. Northern and eastern Lower Michigan were commonly below normal or within one inch of normal. Southern and southwestern Lower Michigan had areas about 1–4 inches above normal.
prcpdev-30days.png.basis: Visual description of the saved MRCC map. Regional values are approximate color-band readings, not station measurements.

prcpdev-90days.png.summary: The Upper Peninsula was generally 2–8 inches below normal. Lower Michigan was mixed: a broad central band and the Thumb were below normal, while parts of the northeast and south were above normal. Most Lower Peninsula departures were within about four inches.
prcpdev-90days.png.basis: Visual description of the saved MRCC map. Regional values are approximate color-band readings, not station measurements.

prcpdev2-7days.png.summary: Much of central and southern Lower Michigan received less than 2% of normal precipitation. Northern Lower Michigan and the eastern Upper Peninsula received larger fractions, commonly 10–50% of normal. No broad Michigan region reaches normal precipitation on this map.
prcpdev2-7days.png.basis: Visual description of the saved MRCC map. Regional values are approximate color-band readings, not station measurements.
prcpdev2-7days.png.dataSource: PRISM Weather Data and NCEI Normals

prcpdev2-30days.png.summary: The Upper Peninsula generally received 10–50% of normal precipitation. Much of northern and eastern Lower Michigan received 50–90%. Southern and southwestern Lower Michigan were near or above normal, with areas at 125–200%.
prcpdev2-30days.png.basis: Visual description of the saved MRCC map. Regional values are approximate color-band readings, not station measurements.
prcpdev2-30days.png.dataSource: PRISM Weather Data and NCEI Normals

prcpdev2-90days.png.summary: The Upper Peninsula generally received 30–75% of normal precipitation. Lower Michigan was mixed: a central band and parts of the Thumb were below normal, while parts of the northeast and south were near or above normal, commonly 100–125%.
prcpdev2-90days.png.basis: Visual description of the saved MRCC map. Regional values are approximate color-band readings, not station measurements.
prcpdev2-90days.png.dataSource: PRISM Weather Data and NCEI Normals

tmax-7days.png.summary: Average daily highs were generally 60–70°F in the Upper Peninsula and northern Lower Michigan, and 65–75°F farther south. Southern Lower Michigan was the warmest part of the state.
tmax-7days.png.basis: Visual description of the saved MRCC map. Regional values are approximate color-band readings, not station measurements.

tmax-30days.png.summary: Average daily highs were generally 60–70°F in the Upper Peninsula, 65–70°F across much of northern and central Lower Michigan, and 70–75°F in the south.
tmax-30days.png.basis: Visual description of the saved MRCC map. Regional values are approximate color-band readings, not station measurements.

tmax-90days.png.summary: Average daily highs were generally 70–75°F across much of the Upper Peninsula, with warmer pockets. Lower Michigan was mostly 75–80°F; some northern areas were 70–75°F.
tmax-90days.png.basis: Visual description of the saved MRCC map. Regional values are approximate color-band readings, not station measurements.

tmaxdev-7days.png.summary: Average daily highs were above the 1991–2020 normal statewide. The Upper Peninsula generally ran 3–12°F warmer, with the larger departures toward the west. Lower Michigan was commonly 3–9°F warmer.
tmaxdev-7days.png.basis: Visual description of the saved MRCC map. Regional values are approximate color-band readings, not station measurements.

tmaxdev-30days.png.summary: Average daily highs were generally 2–6°F above normal in the Upper Peninsula. Lower Michigan was mostly near normal to 2°F above normal, with some warmer areas along the northwest coast.
tmaxdev-30days.png.basis: Visual description of the saved MRCC map. Regional values are approximate color-band readings, not station measurements.

tmaxdev-90days.png.summary: Average daily highs were mostly above normal in the Upper Peninsula, commonly by 1–5°F. Lower Michigan was mostly within about 3°F of normal, with warmer areas in the central and southern peninsula.
tmaxdev-90days.png.basis: Visual description of the saved MRCC map. Regional values are approximate color-band readings, not station measurements.

tmean-7days.png.summary: Mean temperatures were generally 50–55°F across the Upper Peninsula and northern Lower Michigan, with some cooler Upper Peninsula locations. Central and southern Lower Michigan were mostly 55–60°F.
tmean-7days.png.basis: Visual description of the saved MRCC map. Regional values are approximate color-band readings, not station measurements.

tmean-30days.png.summary: Mean temperatures were generally 50–55°F across the Upper Peninsula and parts of northern Lower Michigan. Central Lower Michigan was mostly 55–60°F, and the south was commonly 60–65°F.
tmean-30days.png.basis: Visual description of the saved MRCC map. Regional values are approximate color-band readings, not station measurements.

tmean-90days.png.summary: Mean temperatures were generally 60–65°F in the Upper Peninsula and northern Lower Michigan. Central and southern Lower Michigan were mostly 65–70°F.
tmean-90days.png.basis: Visual description of the saved MRCC map. Regional values are approximate color-band readings, not station measurements.

tmeandev-7days.png.summary: Mean temperatures were generally above the 1991–2020 normal. The western and central Upper Peninsula commonly ran 3–6°F warmer, with some warmer pockets; eastern portions were closer to normal. Lower Michigan was mostly 1–6°F warmer, with locally smaller departures.
tmeandev-7days.png.basis: Visual description of the saved MRCC map. Regional values are approximate color-band readings, not station measurements.

tmeandev-30days.png.summary: Mean temperatures were near normal to about 4°F above normal in the Upper Peninsula. Lower Michigan was mostly within about 2°F of normal, with warmer areas in the southwest and south-central region.
tmeandev-30days.png.basis: Visual description of the saved MRCC map. Regional values are approximate color-band readings, not station measurements.

tmeandev-90days.png.summary: Mean temperatures were generally above normal. The western Upper Peninsula commonly ran 2–4°F warmer; eastern portions were closer to normal. Lower Michigan was mostly near normal to 3°F warmer, with larger departures in parts of the southwest.
tmeandev-90days.png.basis: Visual description of the saved MRCC map. Regional values are approximate color-band readings, not station measurements.

tmin-7days.png.summary: Average daily lows were mostly 35–45°F in the Upper Peninsula. Lower Michigan was mostly 35–45°F inland, with 45–50°F areas along parts of the Lake Michigan coast and the far southwest.
tmin-7days.png.basis: Visual description of the saved MRCC map. Regional values are approximate color-band readings, not station measurements.

tmin-30days.png.summary: Average daily lows were generally 35–45°F in the Upper Peninsula, 40–45°F in northern Lower Michigan, and 45–55°F farther south and along portions of the lakeshores.
tmin-30days.png.basis: Visual description of the saved MRCC map. Regional values are approximate color-band readings, not station measurements.

tmin-90days.png.summary: Average daily lows were generally 45–55°F in the Upper Peninsula. Lower Michigan was mostly 50–55°F in the north and 55–60°F across the central and southern peninsula.
tmin-90days.png.basis: Visual description of the saved MRCC map. Regional values are approximate color-band readings, not station measurements.

tmindev-7days.png.summary: Average daily lows were mixed relative to the 1991–2020 normal. Much of the Upper Peninsula was near normal to 6°F warmer. Lower Michigan had cooler areas in the central interior and southeast, locally 3–6°F below normal, and warmer areas along the Lake Michigan coast.
tmindev-7days.png.basis: Visual description of the saved MRCC map. Regional values are approximate color-band readings, not station measurements.

tmindev-30days.png.summary: Average daily lows were below normal across much of the central and eastern Upper Peninsula, commonly by 2–6°F. Northern and central Lower Michigan also had cooler areas. Southwestern Lower Michigan was warmer, commonly 2–4°F above normal.
tmindev-30days.png.basis: Visual description of the saved MRCC map. Regional values are approximate color-band readings, not station measurements.

tmindev-90days.png.summary: Average daily lows were above normal in much of the western Upper Peninsula but near or slightly below normal in parts of the east. Lower Michigan was mostly near normal to 4°F warmer, with the largest warm departures in the southwest.
tmindev-90days.png.basis: Visual description of the saved MRCC map. Regional values are approximate color-band readings, not station measurements.
